newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti stands firm on budget demands.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti stands firm on budget demands.

text.p: Italy's Fausto Bertinotti, whose Communist Refoundation party is a key government ally, on Friday stood firm on his opposition to social spending cuts and taxes after the government named the day to unveil its mini-budget.

"We believe that any cuts in social spending, any solidarity contributions and any tax rises whatsoever are impossible," Bertinotti told reporters after the government said it would announce details of the financial package next Friday.
Asked whether he feared cuts in pensions or health spending, Bertinotti said: "I'm not afraid because we would be radically opposed and they could not be done."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government relies on support from Bertinotti's hard-left party for a parliamentary majority.

Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said the mini-budget, which the cabinet office said would include deficit-cutting measures of around 15.5 trillion lire, would have "the lowest social impact possible".

Italy needs the mini-budget after an unexpected surge in spending late last year, coupled with a sluggish economy, threatened to wreck Italy's hopes of meeting a three percent deficit-GDP target required to join the European single currency. Veltroni said Italy was now in the "home sprint".
